stories.headline: NFL Week 7: Big takeaways, questions and fantasy spin from Sunday's games
stories.summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 7.
stories.body:
The Sunday slate for Week 7 of the 2026 NFL season kicked off in Paris between the Saints and the Steelers. Pittsburgh dominated in the run game, with Jaylen Warren leading the way on 18 carries for 101 yards, and the Steelers held off New Orleans in the NFL's first game in France.

Later in the afternoon, the Buccaneers dominated the Panthers in QB Baker Mayfield's return, the Vikings remained undefeated and the Bengals handled business in Baltimore.

In the evening slate, the Broncos stole a win in Arizona, and the Lions outlasted the visiting Packers in a duel. The Seahawks finished things off Sunday night by handing the Chiefs their first loss of the season.

Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Michael Florio also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup.

Let's get to it with the biggest lessons from Sunday.

Jump to:

KC-SEA | LAR-LV | GB-DET

DEN-ARI | NYG-HOU | TB-CAR

CLE-TEN | MIA-NYJ | SF-ATL

CIN-BAL | IND-MIN | PIT-NO

Catch up on Thursday's game:

NE-CHI

Seattle 20, Kansas City 3
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap | Instant analysis

Seahawks
Was this a step in the right direction for Sam Darnold? Darnold was rolling in the first half, completing 13 of his first 17 attempts for 178 yards and a touchdown, until he made another mistake that he can't make. His throw on second down into traffic in the back of the end zone during the final seconds of the first half was intercepted, costing Seattle at least three points heading into halftime. That was Darnold's eighth interception over the past five games. Overall, though, this was a better performance for the embattled quarterback (20-of-28 for 257 yards). He got the ball out quickly -- not getting sacked after taking five in each of the previous two games -- and extended plays when he had to.

Key stat to know: Jaxon Smith-Njigba leads the NFL with 867 receiving yards and eight receiving touchdowns. Per ESPN Research, he's the first player in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) with at least 850 receiving yards and eight receiving touchdowns in his team's first seven games of a season. His 129 receiving yards in the first half were the most in any half in his NFL career and the most in any half by a Seahawk since Tyler Lockett in 2020 (133 in the first half at Arizona).

Best quote from the locker room: Smith-Njigba on the Seahawks' mentality entering Sunday's game. "Our backs were against the wall. How we came out here as a brotherhood and fought ... the resiliency of our team is something special, and we're going to keep going."-- Brady Henderson

Next game: vs. Bears (Nov. 2, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Chiefs
Should the Chiefs be looking to trade for receivers? Brett Veach, the Chiefs' general manager, should continue to be interested in acquiring another receiver ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline after the lack of production from the position Sunday. Without Rashee Rice, who missed Sunday's game because of a strained right hamstring, and Tyquan Thornton, who is on the injured reserve list after having surgery to repair his dislocated left ankle, the Chiefs' receivers -- Xavier Worthy, rookie Cyrus Allen, Justin Watson, Andrew Armstrong and Jalen Royals -- produced only six receptions for 39 yards.

Most surprising performance: Entering Sunday, the biggest spotlight was on running back Kenneth Walker III, who became the first Super Bowl MVP to play his former team the next season. Walker also began the week leading the league with 665 rushing yards. The Seahawks, who spent most of the game playing two deep safeties, never allowed Walker to rush for at least 10 yards on a single carry. Walker finished the game with just 36 yards on 14 carries. -- Nate Taylor

Next game: at Broncos (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Patrick Mahomes' fantasy struggles continued, as he scored a season-low six fantasy points. He threw for only 165 yards and has topped 250 passing yards once in his past four games, and has not thrown a touchdown in either of his past two games. Overall, he has averaged 12.4 fantasy points per game in his past four games and is not a must-start option at the moment. Fantasy managers might want to avoid next week's matchup against Denver if they have another viable QB option. -- Florio

L.A. Rams 35, Las Vegas 21
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Rams
Will leaning on Puka Nacua and tight ends be the Rams' offensive identity without Davante Adams? Outside of Nacua, just one Rams wide receiver had a catch: Konata Mumpfield, for 15 yards. Instead, the Rams turned to their tight ends (Davis Allen, Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee) and their running backs (Kyren Williams and Blake Corum). It led to their highest-scoring game of the season. Most of the points came in the first half, when Los Angeles scored on four-straight possessions. The Rams will be without Adams, who injured a hamstring in Week 6, for another five to nine weeks.

Key stat to know: After fumbling on the Rams' second drive of the second half, Williams has nine lost fumbles since becoming the Rams starter in 2023. According to ESPN Research, that is the most of any running back over the span. -- Sarah Barshop

Next game: vs. Chargers (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Raiders
Is the clock ticking on Kirk Cousins' time as a starter? Not necessarily. The Raiders have lost four straight and are below .500 for the first time this season. Sure, Cousins didn't have his best game overall. He missed open targets a fair amount of time, and his lack of mobility was noticeable. But he has not been the sole problem during his team's losing skid. He threw a pair of touchdowns in the fourth quarter, increasing his season total to 16. Cousins has his limitations, which are exposed when frequently blitzed, as he was Sunday. At the same time, he hasn't done anything major that's worth making a switch for No. 1 draft pick Fernando Mendoza.

Trend to watch: Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard's seat might start feeling a bit warm. The Raiders have allowed 30-plus points for the fourth straight game. Since Week 3, Las Vegas is last in points (34) and total yards (405.4) allowed. Yes, the Raiders have gone against tough QBs. But that's not an excuse for their inability to generate consistent pressure or stop the run. -- Ryan McFadden

Next game: at Jets (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: In the Rams' first game without Adams, we saw more tight end usage from coach Sean McVay, but the key fantasy targets haven't changed. Nacua (21.8 points), Williams (18.1 points) and QB Matthew Stafford (17.5 points) led the way, while Corum (17.1 points) continues to provide solid flex value. -- Bowen

Detroit 20, Green Bay 17
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Lions
Has the Lions' defense turned the corner? Detroit's D entered the week as one of the worst units in the NFL, and Sunday's prospects against a surging Packers offense looked daunting. But the defense held strong. Detroit allowed just 17 points, forced a turnover -- by recently returned DB Brian Branch -- and held Green Bay to 5-of-15 on third down. Couple Sunday's performance with an encouraging effort against the Cardinals before the Lions' bye and there's two weeks of evidence that D-coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's troops might finally be trending in the right direction.

Trend to watch: Wideout Jameson Williams is becoming more of a focal point in the offense. His two touchdown catches Sunday made him the third player this season with multiple receiving TDs in back-to-back games, joining teammate Amon-Ra St. Brown and Seattle's Jaxon Smith-Njigba. -- ESPN Staff

Next game: vs. Vikings (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Packers
Where are the Packers in the NFC North pecking order? The short answer: They're in trouble. Yes, the NFC North looks like one of the best divisions -- if not the best -- in the NFL. All four teams have winning records. But after playing each team in the division once, the Packers are at the bottom. They're just 1-2 against NFC North teams. What's worse is the Packers couldn't win a game that the Lions tried to give away with fumbles and questionable decisions. Green Bay's only NFC North victory came at home against a backup quarterback because Bears starter Caleb Williams was out with a hamstring injury.

Trend to watch: Running back Josh Jacobs looked rusty in his first game of the season. Aside from a 25-yard catch and run for a score, he left plays on the field, including a drop on what would have been the go-ahead touchdown with 3:25 remaining in the contest. -- Rob Demovsky

Next game: vs. Panthers (Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Jacobs made his return, playing 54% of the snaps with 11 carries for 36 yards. He added five catches for 55 yards and a touchdown -- nearly catching a second -- on seven targets, finishing with 20.1 fantasy points. His workload will likely increase moving forward. He is a must-start option Thursday against the visiting Panthers, who allow a league-high 127 rushing yards per game to RBs. -- Florio

Denver 30, Arizona 16
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Broncos
Is Denver's offense getting better? The Broncos flashed, with three plays of at least 47 yards. But as the fourth quarter began, about half of the Broncos' output came on those plays (a 60-yard TD run by Bo Nix, a 52-yard catch and run for a TD by RJ Harvey, and a 47-yard reception by Marvin Mims Jr.). Overall, beyond even Denver's 114 yards in penalties, third down is still an immense struggle; the offense still had four possessions that were 16 or fewer yards; and Nix (15-of-29 passing) still looks unsettled. The Broncos avoided the proverbial trap game -- with Kansas City next -- and the big plays were a welcome sight for them. They still need to be far better with the ball.

Trend to watch: Since coach Sean Payton took back playcalling duties in Week 5, the offense has gotten worse on third down. Denver was 4-of-26 (15.4%) on third down in the two games combined before Sunday. Add Sunday's 3-of-11 showing to the pile and the offense continues to be mired in its inability to maintain possessions or find any semblance of sequencing. -- Jeff Legwold

Next game: vs. Chiefs (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Cardinals
How do the Cardinals start scoring touchdowns? Something drastic needs to happen -- and quickly. Arizona has registered just one touchdown in its past two games. It's also 1-for-10 in the red zone over that span, with the lone touchdown -- and Arizona's only TD of the game -- coming Sunday from Trey McBride. The issues were exacerbated late in the fourth quarter when Arizona had seven plays to score and didn't. The Cardinals need to give QB Jacoby Brissett more time; he was hit 10 times on Sunday. They also need to figure out ways to get their stars, including McBride and Michael Wilson, more involved in the red zone.

Key stat to know: The Cardinals were 5-for-17 on third down -- a 29% clip -- on Sunday against Denver, highlighting their inability to get must-needed yards in crucial situations. -- Josh Weinfuss

Next game: at Cowboys (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Nix posted his best game of the campaign with 26.28 points. He threw for 222 yards and one touchdown and added 74 rushing yards and a 62-yard scoring run. The 12.2 fantasy points on that TD run alone are more than what he tallied in three separate games this season. Do not be fooled by the one play: This was an encouraging first step, but fantasy managers need to see more before trusting him again. -- Florio

N.Y. Giants 27, Houston 21
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Giants
What did J.J. McCarthy bring to the Giants' offense? McCarthy's performance was impressive. His composure was obvious while completing 20 of 28 passes for 252 yards. Coach John Harbaugh said during the week it was "evident" that this was the "right time" to make the switch from Jameis Winston to McCarthy. That proved to be the right call: McCarthy was in control the entire contest against Houston. He led seven drives into Texans territory. More than anything, McCarthy added explosiveness to the Giants' offense. They had five pass plays of 20-plus yards and used McCarthy's big arm for five attempts of over 20-plus air yards. It opened up the run game as well, which produced a Cam Skattebo 42-yard run and Devin Singletary's game-winning 30-yard TD in overtime.

Trend to watch: Deonte Banks' strong coverage. The rejuvenated Giants cornerback locked up Texans top receiver Nico Collins most of the afternoon. The Texans completed just four of seven passes for 25 yards when throwing in Banks' direction, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. Collins finished with two catches on five targets for 6 yards, thanks in large part to Banks. -- Jordan Raanan

Next game: at Eagles (Nov. 8, 1 p.m. ET)

Texans
Are the Texans' playoffs chances dead? Never say never with Houston under coach DeMeco Ryans, but the chances are dwindling after their loss to the Giants. According to ESPN Research, the Texans' chances of making the playoffs shrunk to 31%. It was a combination of everything that cost Houston on Sunday, including an ineffective running game (3.4 yards per carry) and stellar performances by McCarthy (20-of-28 for 252 yards) and Skattebo (124 rushing yards). You name something bad, the Texans probably did it on Sunday.

Trend to watch: Is Houston's defense just bad? The Texans have allowed at least 27 points in four outings this season. And it wasn't only against upper-echelon quarterbacks; on Sunday it was against McCarthy in his first start as a Giant. It's panic time in Houston. -- DJ Bien-Aime

Next game: at Chargers (Nov. 8, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: McCarthy had a good real-life game. It did not translate into a big fantasy performance (10.18 fantasy points), but he showed that the Giants' top options remain fantasy relevant. Malik Nabers finished with 11 targets, seven catches and 111 yards (18.1 fantasy points) and remains a must-start WR1. Skattebo rushed 17 times for 124 yards and a touchdown and is back in the RB2/flex range. -- Florio

Tampa Bay 43, Carolina 13
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Buccaneers
What does this divisional win mean for the Bucs? At 2-5, the Bucs are fighting to get to the top of the NFC South. Quarterback Baker Mayfield didn't have to do much with his injured right thumb (just 11 passing attempts). Tampa Bay had 258 yards on the ground, including three touchdowns. The defense sacked Bryce Young five times and picked him off twice. And special teams (their most-maligned unit last season) recovered a muffed punt and blocked an extra point attempt that Zyon McCollum returned for two points. The Bucs could gain more divisional ground next week if they're willing to test a weak Falcons secondary through the air.

What to make of the QB performance: In his return from a dislocated right thumb, Mayfield completed 7 of 11 passes for 64 yards and a touchdown. His workload was modest, but his third-down throw to Tez Johnson along the sideline, and later a 14-yard touchdown off his back foot, showed what he can still do unscripted. -- Jenna Laine

Next game: vs. Falcons (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Panthers
Can the Panthers bounce back quickly for "Thursday Night Football"? The Buccaneers had been slumping, and Mayfield had an injured throwing thumb, and yet the Panthers looked obsolete on their home turf. On a day when franchise legend Luke Kuechly was honored at halftime, everything that could go wrong went wrong for Carolina. Special teams had a pair of embarrassing blunders that led to points for the Bucs. Young coughed up the ball three times in the first three quarters. The defense gave up 322 net yards and four TDs. The Panthers will have just a few days to recover before Thursday's game.

Key stat to know: The Panthers gave up 22 points off miscues in the first three quarters. A muffed punt and a blocked extra point attempt on special teams led to five points for Tampa Bay. A trio of turnovers by Young (a sack-fumble and two interceptions) led to 17 points for the Bucs. -- Mike Kaye

Best quote out of the locker room: Panthers tight end Tommy Tremble didn't hold back on the miscues that snowballed for the Panthers in a blowout loss Sunday: "When we turn the ball over ... make mistakes like that, it's really tough to win in this league. Everyone's a professional, everyone's good at their job. And so, we gave them the upper leg and [they] didn't let go of it. So, it was a tough result because of that."

Next game: at Packers (Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Buccaneers RB Bucky Irving had himself a day, turning 26 opportunities into 110 yards and two touchdowns and finishing with 24 fantasy points. Irving has been up and down this season but has shown the capability to take advantage of positive matchups. He is back to must-start status off volume alone. -- Florio

Cleveland 27, Tennessee 24
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Browns
Did the Browns finally unlock their running game? It sure seems like it after a season-high 183 rushing yards against the Titans. With the return of Quinshon Judkins (96 yards) and Dylan Sampson (45 yards), Cleveland had a good mix of runs from under center, shotgun and the pistol. Quarterback Deshaun Watson's 9-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter was also a reminder of the impact he can have with his legs.

Key stat to know: Browns wide receiver KC Concepcion joined Odell Beckham Jr. as one of two rookies since 2000 with eight-plus receptions and 125-plus receiving yards in the first half of a game. Concepcion finished the game with a career-high eight receptions for 129 yards. -- Daniel Oyefusi

Best quote out of the locker room: "I got to give the fans something to watch and enjoy. It boosts the NFL ratings, so I know they loving that," cornerback Denzel Ward said on Cleveland's string of late-game wins.

Next game: at Steelers (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Titans
Is it time for the Titans' offense to go through the rushing attack? The offense finished with 24 points but didn't score in the second or third quarter and squandered a 14-point lead. Quarterback Cam Ward was picked off immediately after a turnover that gave the Titans the ball in plus territory. Tony Pollard and the offensive line held their own throughout, leading to 141 rushing yards and three touchdowns. Coach Robert Saleh said the offensive identity needs to be the run game. He's right. The Titans can't rely on a passing game that ranked dead last, averaging only 153.5 yards per game, entering this week.

Key stat to know: The Titans tied the Browns for the NFL's longest streak of games between consecutive wins. Cleveland went 65 games between November 2014 and September 2018. The Titans haven't won consecutive games dating to November 2022. -- Turron Davenport

Next game: at Bengals (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Judkins scored a season-high 23.4 points, rushing for 96 yards and two touchdowns on 17 carries plus a reception for 8 yards. Yes, Judkins is a touchdown-dependent player in the lineup, but he has had two goal-to-go rushes in two of his past three games, and he sees the Steelers' defense again in Week 8. He should be locked in as RB2 for that one. -- Bowen

Miami 28, N.Y. Jets 25
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Dolphins
Was the Dolphins' 0-5 start a reflection of their quality or the quality of their opponents? A little of each, but two of their first five games were against undefeated teams in the Chiefs and Vikings (that list would have included the 49ers before Sunday's loss). Dolphins players have said multiple times that they needed to learn how to win games, and linebacker Jordyn Brooks said they could do so by getting tired of losing. Miami looked tired of losing this week, particularly as the Jets mounted a late comeback. The Dolphins still have a way to go before pulling themselves out of the NFL's cellar, but you could sense a win was coming based on how they've played over their past four games.

What to make of the QB performance: Malik Willis played the best half of football we've seen from him this season -- leading the Dolphins to a 21-7 halftime lead. He was decisive and accurate through the air and efficient when he scrambled. His best moment might have been sliding inbounds on a short scramble in the first half, which allowed the clock to keep running. That heads-up play kept Miami's 15-play, 91-yard scoring drive alive and showed his ability to think calmly in the heat of the moment. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques

Next game: vs. Patriots (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Jets
What does this loss mean for coach Aaron Glenn's job security? It will be tough for Glenn -- 5-19 overall and 0-8 in the AFC East -- to come back from this one. This was a major step back for a coach whose job security is predicated on demonstrating progress. Even if the Jets split their remaining games to finish 7-10 -- unlikely, considering the team's wildly erratic play -- will that be enough to warrant another season? Facing the previously winless Dolphins, the Jets were exposed in so many ways, mainly on defense, which is Glenn's calling card. Quite frankly, this was one of the worst losses in recent Jets history. It looks bleak for Glenn.

Trend to watch: Wide receiver Garrett Wilson (two catches, three targets) was a nonfactor for the second week in a row. His frustration erupted in the fourth quarter as TV cameras caught him yelling at QB Geno Smith on the bench. Both players denied it. The Smith-Wilson chemistry leaves a lot to be desired, and it's hurting the overall offense. -- Rich Cimini

Best quote out of the locker room: "I understand the fans' frustration -- I really do. I promise you. I do -- but the thing is, I do feel like, man, this program is going in the right direction," Glenn said.

Next game: vs. Raiders (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Willis had his best game of the year with 26 fantasy points. It was his first game with multiple passing touchdowns and his second straight game throwing and running for a touchdown. He has three rushing TDs and has run for at least 37 yards in four of six games. His rushing ability is making him a fantasy QB2 who can be streamed in the right matchups, and his schedule opens up after Week 8. -- Florio

Atlanta 29, San Francisco 20
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Falcons
Have the Falcons figured out their offensive formula? Atlanta has flashed a potent offense before, but in those games -- wins over the Packers and Saints -- it was carried by running back Bijan Robinson and wide receiver Drake London. On Sunday, quarterback Michael Penix Jr. got contributions from a host of players, including a third straight game with a touchdown for tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. Even Nick Muse, the team's fourth tight end, caught a touchdown pass, the first of his career. The Falcons offense looked very West Coast against the Niners, ironically. Going into the fourth quarter, 20 of Penix's 29 pass attempts were 5 air yards or fewer.

What to make of the QB performance: The scouting report on Penix coming in was that he struggled under pressure. The 49ers, though, were barely able to get close to him. Penix was pressured on three of his 34 dropbacks (9%) - that's the lowest pressure percentage by a 49ers team in a game since Week 16 of 2024. Penix ended up 25-of-34 passing for 213 yards with three touchdowns. -- Marc Raimondi

Next game: at Buccaneers (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

49ers
How badly do the 49ers need their Week 8 bye after their first loss? Desperately -- and that isn't an overstatement given the issues laid bare in Sunday's defeat. The timing of the bye with the Nov. 10 trade deadline approaching should boost the team's the desire to make moves sooner rather than later. San Francisco expects to welcome DE Nick Bosa; WRs Mike Evans, Demarcus Robinson and Deebo Samuel Sr.; CB Upton Stout; and S Marques Sigle back from injury soon after the bye. That will help in a lot of ways but the lack of pass rush against Atlanta should serve as an impetus for the Niners to make a meaningful addition or two on the defensive line in the coming weeks.

Most surprising performance: The whole team. Through their 6-0 start, the 49ers have avoided big mistakes, but they were guilty of many on Sunday. That included a pair of costly interceptions, two fumbles, silly penalties at inopportune times and more special teams struggles. Perhaps they were due for a clunker, but 7-0 was there for the taking if they'd at least played a clean game. -- Nick Wagoner

Next game: vs. Raiders (Nov. 8, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: After a rough start to the season, this Falcons passing game is settling in with Penix under center, which creates more consistent opportunities for London. In Sunday's win over the 49ers, London scored 19.6 points and caught his first touchdown of the season, and he's had 18 or more points in three of his past five games. London fits as a lower-tier WR1 for Week 8. -- Bowen

Cincinnati 35, Baltimore 13
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Bengals
Could this win jump-start Cincinnati's season? It certainly could have that effect. Between last season's final meeting against the Ravens and the first half of Sunday's game, Cincinnati was outscored 34-0 by Baltimore and looked lifeless. But things flipped for the Bengals in the second half. Cincinnati scored 35 straight points and later iced the game with an interception by linebacker Demetrius Knight Jr. It was a gut-check performance for the Bengals, who couldn't afford to lose to a Ravens team playing without quarterback Lamar Jackson (ankle).

What to make of the QB performance: Joe Burrow was absolutely sublime in the second half. After the offense posted the lowest yardage total of his career (59 yards) in the first half, Burrow led the offense on five straight TD drives in the second half. He was 22-of-30 passing for 292 yards and four TDs in a resounding and needed win. -- Ben Baby

Next game: vs. Titans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Ravens
Are the Ravens already out of the AFC North race? Baltimore fell to 0-2 in the AFC North for the first time in 19 years. Since the formation of the AFC North in 2002, only one team has started 0-2 in the division and went on to win it (2022 Bengals). The biggest issue is the lack of explosiveness without Jackson. Tyler Huntley went 8-of-13 for 62 yards with a fumble and an interception in the second half. In 14 quarters with Jackson this season, the Ravens have scored 116 points and 14 offensive touchdowns. In 14 quarters with Huntley, Baltimore has totaled 53 points and five touchdowns. There is hope that Jackson can return next Sunday, but it could be too late to make up ground in the AFC North.

Trend to watch: The Ravens continue to be the NFL's best at blowing leads. After failing to hold a 13-0 halftime lead, Baltimore has now blown 17 double-digit leads since 2020, which are the most in the NFL. In all three losses this season -- Saints, Browns and Bengals -- the Ravens have held double-digit leads. -- Jamison Hensley

Next game: at Bills (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Ravens RB Derrick Henry failed to post double-digit points for the second straight game, rushing for 45 yards on 17 carries while adding one reception for four yards (5.9 fantasy points). Henry is seeing consistent volume (at least 18 touches in every game in 2026) but he has been inefficient on goal line opportunities, and his lack of receiving usage caps his ceiling. Henry should be viewed a touchdown dependent, lower-tier RB1 for Week 8. -- Bowen

Minnesota 16, Indianapolis 10
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Vikings
Why did the Vikings' offense struggle? This was supposed to be a big day. Most of the Vikings' injured offensive players returned to the field, giving them a nearly full complement of running backs, receivers and tight ends. But if it weren't for quarterback Kyler Murray's 35-yard scramble to convert a third down on the first play of the fourth quarter, it's possible the Vikings would have failed to score a touchdown in a game for the third time this season. They seemed out of sync from the start, when coach Kevin O'Connell called four consecutive runs for Aaron Jones Sr., and never found a rhythm. It was enough to get through Sunday but certainly doesn't look playoff-caliber.

Most surprising performance: Linebacker Blake Cashman. He is having a strong season in a contract year, but Sunday's effort was arguably beyond anything he has produced in his eight-year career. He affected the Colts' passing game from all angles, finishing with two sacks, four pass breakups and 12 tackles. -- Kevin Seifert

Next game: at Lions (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Colts
Will the Colts find any offensive traction this season? It's difficult to judge an offense against the blitz-crazy Vikings' defense, but it's hard to win with a quarterback who had fewer than 100 passing yards prior to the game's final drive. Daniel Jones was under pressure at times in the game, with Minnesota registering 10 quarterback hits. But he was also responsible for some of that by holding the ball in the pocket and allowing pass rushers time to beat their blockers. On the positive side, Jones didn't commit any turnovers until the final last-gasp series. But when he avoids risk, that presents its own set of problems.

Most surprising performance: Defensive tackle Adetomiwa Adebawore. He continued to make waves even in his part-time role. He registered two sacks on Sunday and harassed Vikings QB Kyler Murray throughout the game. He also was a factor in the run game, chasing down running back Aaron Jones Sr. on a sweep from the backside of the defense for a minimal gain. Adebawore now has four sacks this season, matching a career high. -- Stephen Holder

Next game: at Jaguars (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Vikings RB Jordan Mason returned, playing 63% of snaps and getting 15 carries for 68 yards and just 6.8 fantasy points. Aaron Jones Sr. did get the start and the bulk of the work on the opening drive, but Mason saw more after that. Mason, who is a better fit in the Vikings' rushing attack, is still a flex option moving forward. He would elevate to RB2 if Jones, who exited in the fourth quarter with an injury, were to miss time. -- Florio

Pittsburgh 16, New Orleans 10
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Steelers
Are the Steelers embracing their RB-led identity on offense? This game was right on time for the Steelers, whose running game properly supported their 42-year-old quarterback with 5.4 yards per carry. Jaylen Warren is the Steelers' best offensive player. Opposing coaches agree. And, for the fourth game this season, he produced 125-plus scrimmage yards, tying Kansas City's Kenneth Walker III for most in the NFL. This offensive line is opening holes for Warren and Rico Dowdle, the bruising complement to Warren's burst. They closed out the game late, and Pittsburgh ran 12 plays for 79 yards with six offensive linemen on the field today (had zero such plays entering the game). The passing game needs more explosive plays. But the running game can handle the rest.

Trend to watch: The Steelers' second-half adjustments defensively were encouraging. The Steelers were blitz-heavy in the first half, coming for quarterback Tyler Shough 50% of the time. Shough went 9-of-10 for 98 yards and a TD on those plays. So, defensive coordinator Patrick Graham dropped the Steelers into coverage more often in the second half, blitzing twice on 21 attempts -- both blitzes coming on the Saints' failed final offensive drive. Timely defense for the Steelers, who held the Saints to 18 rushing yards, the fewest for New Orleans since 1999. -- Jeremy Fowler

Next game: vs. Browns (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Saints
Can the Saints get healthy and get help coming out of their Week 8 bye? New Orleans quarterback Tyler Shough entered Sunday's game with an injured non-throwing hand, and he appeared to take a hit on his throwing hand as well. Shough could likely use the week of rest to get healthy, but he's not the only one. The Saints don't have a run game and have relied heavily on Shough. Could running back Travis Etienne and wide receiver Jordyn Tyson make their debuts after the bye to give the Saints much-needed help? The Saints are also missing left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr., who went on injured reserve in late September following ankle surgery.

What to make of the QB performance: Shough was playing injured and without the benefit of a run game, and he tried to put the game on his shoulders. That had mixed results, as the 27-year-old turned the ball over with a red zone interception but also threw for 278 yards and a touchdown. -- Katherine Terrell

Next game: vs. Browns (Nov. 8, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Steelers RB Jaylen Warren led the Pittsburgh backfield with 21 touches for 137 total yards (16.7 fantasy points), and he'll remain a weekly RB2. Rico Dowdle also played a key role, rushing for 41 yards on nine carries while adding six receptions for 45 yards (14.6 fantasy points). Given the structure of this Pittsburgh system -- which is based on run game volume and quick passing -- Dowdle projects to have flex value moving forward. -- Bowen

stories.headline: Quinn Hughes has a goal and an assist in his Vancouver return in Wild's 4-2 victory
stories.summary: — Former Vancouver captain Quinn Hughes had a goal to reach 500 NHL points and added an assist in his return to Rogers Arena in the Minnesota Wild’s 4-2 victory over the Canucks on Sunday night.
stories.body:
VANCOUVER, British Columbia -- — Former Vancouver captain Quinn Hughes had a goal to reach 500 NHL points and added an assist in his return to Rogers Arena in the Minnesota Wild’s 4-2 victory over the Canucks on Sunday night.


Traded to Minnesota in December, Hughes was booed throughout the night.


He scored on a power player midway through the second period to make it 3-0, and set up Kirill Kaprizov’s NHL-leading 13th goal early in the third for a 4-0 advantage. In 13 games this season, Hughes has three goals and 13 assists.


Picked seventh overall by the Canucks in 2018, Hughes played 6 1/2 seasons in Vancouver before the blockbuster trade sent him to Minnesota. The deal saw Vancouver acquire Marco Rossi and Liam Ohgren, defenseman Zeev Buium and the Wild’s first-round pick in the 2026 NHL draft.


Kaprizov and Maxim Shabanov also each had a goal and assist, and Bobby Brink scored.


Calvin Pickard made 15 saves as the Wild improved to 8-3-2, following up a 5-1 victory over the Kraken in Seattle on Saturday.


Max Sasson and Brock Boeser scored for Vancouver. Leevi Merilainen stopped 30 shots.


Vancouver dropped to 2-10-1 with its 10th straight loss.


Hughes became the second-fastest American defenseman to reach 500 NHL points, achieving the feat in 520 games. Brian Leetch hit the milestone in 496 games with the New York Rangers.


Up next

Wild: At Utah on Tuesday night.


Canucks: At Anaheim on Tuesday night.

stories.headline: Consensus top AFL draft prospect Dougie Cochrane already in rare air
stories.summary: Missing significant chunks of football hasn't stopped Port Adelaide NGA star Dougie Cochrane from firming as the top prospect in this year's AFL Draft.
stories.body:
It's rare for a player to be the consensus no. 1 rated prospect in their draft. From coaches to recruiters and a myriad of draft evaluators, Dougie Cochrane stands atop 2026's crop. For him to do so after playing just four games in his top-age campaign puts the Port Adelaide NGA gun in rare air.

The starring junior missed both years of his u18 national championships through injury, and this year only returned to the field in the final month of the season. But what he produced at league level last season and amongst his peers at the u16s national championships in 2024 is not easily forgotten.

Clearly a class above at the national championships three years ago, Cochrane put all of his skill and athleticism on show. He was a distributor out of defence, won aerial duels around the ground and was the focal point of the SA forward line in a showing of his unique versatility.

From there he made his league debut for Central Districts as a 17-year-old, kicking four goals including an outrageous snap on his left foot from the pocket after crumbing a forward 50 contest. From his first game he was already the best player on the ground.

Speaking to ESPN ahead of the draft combine Cochrane was a bit flat. It wasn't because he'd missed his top-age season, he knew he wasn't going to be testing, and he knew most clubs wouldn't bother booking an interview given his ties to Port Adelaide. But there was one thing that really got to him.

"They measured me at 194-and-a-half centimetres," he tells ESPN with a grin. "They took a centimetre off me, but we'll round that up."

At six-foot-four (we'll round it up too) he's widely considered the next elite key forward prospect to come through the AFL Draft. Only he doesn't necessarily see it that way.

"I want to be a midfielder when I'm older, that's what I'm striving towards. "For right now I'm pretty happy forward, if not back. I'm happy wherever the team needs, whatever the team needs.

"I'm pretty skinny right now, I'm not as muscly as the Patty Cripps's of the world, the Bonts of the world. I want to focus on my midfield craft and get that experience."

Cochrane missed a significant chunk of his bottom-age year with a hamstring and over the off-season underwent knee surgery to address patella tendinitis. He didn't play for 11 straight months from the end of 2025 to July 2026.

Watching from the sidelines frustrated him but he knew it was all out of an abundance of caution.

"I started playing league at Centrals last year, I sort of started feeling [knee pain] a little bit. I thought nothing of it, just thought it was a bit of growing pain. It got worse and worse by the time I started doing pre-season... when you take off and do your powerful stuff it flares up.

"They did a clean out of it... I had the surgery, and I walked out of the surgery. It was two little key holes."

Cochrane sat down with ESPN as Port Adelaide list manager Jason Cripps all but confirmed on Trade Radio Essendon would be bidding on the gun academy prospect at pick one in the 2026 AFL Draft.

He's the son of Port Adelaide and North Melbourne midfielder Stuart Cochrane, and grew up supporting the Power after his dad's playing career finished up. His brother Tom was on the list during formative years and the club is set up to match his bid wherever it lands.

"Dad's been my idol growing up. Looking up to him, I obviously didn't get to see him play but he's been enormous."

Asked if it would mean more being that first selection on November 19, Cochrane's humble nature shines through.

"I loved watching the draft growing up, seeing those high picks. The pick doesn't really matter, does it? There have been a lot of picks over times where the number one picks haven't gone as well as they should've. I just want to end up at an AFL club - wherever that is I don't mind - but I just want to play footy," he says.

"Growing up and supporting Port all my life, it would be special playing for them. But whatever happens happens and I'm just gonna let that decide itself."

stories.headline: Golden State, Atlanta tied 2-2 heading into game 5
stories.summary: Atlanta Dream (30-14, 15-5 Eastern Conference) at Golden State Valkyries (32-12, 15-8 Western Conference)
stories.body:
Atlanta Dream (30-14, 15-5 Eastern Conference) at Golden State Valkyries (32-12, 15-8 Western Conference)

San Francisco; Monday, 8 p.m. EDT

LINE: Valkyries -1.5; over/under is 150.5

WNBA FINALS: Series tied 2-2

BOTTOM LINE: The Atlanta Dream visit the Golden State Valkyries for game five of the WNBA Finals with the series tied 2-2. The Valkyries beat the Dream 67-62 in the last matchup. Gabby Williams led the Valkyries with 17 points, and Rhyne Howard led the Dream with 19 points.

The Valkyries have gone 17-5 at home. Golden State leads the WNBA allowing only 75.1 points per game while holding opponents to 41.4% shooting.

stories.headline: Bruno Fernandes' home burgled during Man United loss against Como
stories.summary: Bruno Fernandes returned from Italy after losing to Como with Manchester United in the early hours of Thursday morning and had to deal with a robbery at his house.
stories.body:
Police are investigating a burglary at Bruno Fernandes' home which took place as he returned from Italy with Manchester United after losing to Como.

Fernandes' family are understood not to have been in the house at the time and police quickly attended the scene, with United supporting their skipper.

A statement from Cheshire Police, given to ESPN, read: "At around 8.30 p.m. on Wednesday Oct. 21, police were called to reports of suspicious activity at an address in the Alderley Park area of Nether Alderley.

"The caller reported three unknown men in the rear garden of a neighbouring property.

"Officers attended the scene and on arrival there was no trace of the suspects. However, officers discovered that there had been a burglary at the address and a number of items had been stolen.

"An investigation into the incident has been launched and enquiries are ongoing."

Detective Inspector David Jarvis of Macclesfield Proactive CID said: "This investigation is in its early stages at this time, and we're committed to doing all we can to trace the people responsible.

"As part of our enquiries were keen to hear from anyone who was in the local area at the time and believes they may have witnessed anything suspicious.

"The same goes for anyone with any CCTV or dashcam footage which may aid the investigation."

Bruno Fernandes questions Man United tactics

A catastrophic night in Lombardy saw United suffer a humiliating 4-1 loss to Cesc Fabregas' side, which extended their winless run to seven fixtures and led to Fernandes publicly questioning the approach of boss Michael Carrick.

- Wayne Rooney: Bruno Fernandes, Man United players acting like 'babies'

- Who's to blame for Man United mess: Carrick, the players ... Ratcliffe?

- Cesc Fàbregas: I told Como players to 'slow down' in closing stages of Man United win

The result, alongside Fernandes' comments, had raised serious questions about Carrick's future ahead of Sunday's Premier League home game against Bournemouth, but he will remain in charge for that match, sources told ESPN.

United skipper Fernandes has been a pale imitation of last season's performer so far this term, and questioned Carrick's tactics as another Champions League trip ended with an eye-catching post-match player interview following on from last week's remarks by Lisandro Martínez.

Fernandes claimed it was the staff's decision "not to press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind" in Como.

Information from ESPN's Rob Dawson, and the Press Association, contributed to this report.
